name: Diotimus of Miletus
bio: Diotimus of Miletus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 3rd century BC. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 3 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book V: 106; Book VI: 267, 358).

poems.title: Book V, 106
poems.author: Diotimus of Miletus
poems.text: Granny, dear nurse, why do you bark at me when I approach, and cast me into torments twice as cruel. You accompany a lovely girl, and look how treading in her steps I go my own way, only gazing at her sweet form. Why be jealous of eyes, ill-fated nurse? We are allowed to look on the forms of even the immortals.

poems.title: Book VI, 267
poems.author: Diotimus of Miletus
poems.text: Stand here, Artemis the Saviour, with thy torch on the land of Pollis, and give thy delightful light to him and to his children. The task is easy ; for no feeble knowledge hath he from Zeus of the unerring scales of Justice. And, Artemis, let the Graces too race over this grove, treading on the flowers with their light sandals.

poems.title: Book VI, 358
poems.author: Diotimus of Miletus
poems.text: Hail, dainty frock, that Lydian Omphale doffed to goto the bed of Heracles. Thou wert blessed then, O frock, and blessed again art thou now that thou hast entered this golden house of Artemis.
